cards.title: 提格雷武装发动新攻势并组建反政府联盟，埃塞俄比亚濒临内战重启

entities.name: 提格雷人民解放阵线（TPLF）
entities.explain: 埃塞俄比亚北部提格雷地区的政党和武装组织，曾长期主导国家政治，2020-2022年与联邦政府爆发全面战争

entities.name: 阿比·艾哈迈德
entities.explain: 埃塞俄比亚现任总理，2019年诺贝尔和平奖得主，2020年对提格雷发动军事行动

entities.name: 阿法尔和阿姆哈拉
entities.explain: 埃塞俄比亚北部两个州，与提格雷州相邻，是当前战事蔓延的地区

cards.summary: 提格雷武装力量向邻接的阿法尔和阿姆哈拉州发动攻势，并联合其他反政府力量组建新联盟，目标推翻阿比·艾哈迈德政府。双方互相指责对方破坏停火。2020至2022年的内战已造成约60万人死亡，外界担忧大规模冲突将再度爆发。
cards.relevant: 埃塞俄比亚是非洲人口第二大国，若再次陷入全面内战，将引发严重的人道主义危机并动摇整个非洲之角的地缘稳定。
cards.context: 2022年埃塞俄比亚联邦政府与TPLF签署和平协议结束了两年内战，但协议核心条款（如武装解除、领土争议）执行不力，双方信任持续恶化，最终导致提格雷方面重新发动军事行动。
cards.source_analysis: 《卫报》长期关注非洲冲突与人道议题，报道倾向对阿比政府持批评立场，强调平民伤亡和战争风险。
cards.social_impact: 上一轮内战已致约60万人死亡，数百万人流离失所。新一轮攻势可能波及阿法尔和阿姆哈拉等邻近州，影响数百万平民。
cards.source_text: There are growing fears of a return to civil war in Ethiopia after an offensive by fighters from Tigray into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara and the formation of a new rebel alliance aimed at overthrowing the government of the prime minister, Abiy Ahmed. About 600,000 people died between 2020 and 2022 during a devastating war between the Ethiopian army and the political party and paramilitary group the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). Both sides are now accusing the other of triggering a return to open conflict. On Sunday, seven armed groups from around the country, including the TPLF, announced the formation of the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, aimed at deposing the government in Addis Ababa. Then, on Wednesday, the TPLF seized control of three airports from federal police. The state-owned carrier, Ethiopian Airlines, said it had suspended flights to the region “due to the current situation”. The TPLF also launched attacks into Afar and Amhara. A humanitarian source in Afar told Agence France-Presse there were heavy artillery attacks by the group on Thursday as they attempted to take control of the town of Yallo, near the Tigrayan border. Flights to the historic Ethiopian town of Lalibela were also suspended on Thursday because of nearby fighting, while people in Tigray stocked up on food and cash, with one resident telling Reuters that people there feared they could face siege conditions similar to those during the previous war. A resident of Adigrat, a city close to the Eritrean border, described panic-buying and shops emptying. “Food shortages are worsening as market shelves sit empty … Essential medicines remain scarce and astronomically expensive,” he told Reuters. “Daily survival has become a constant calculation.” The TPLF’s vice-president, Amanuel Assefa, told AFP: “We are in the situation of full-blown war now.” He confirmed Tigrayan forces were fighting alongside local armed groups in Afar and Amhara. The group took control of Abala, also on the Tigray-Afar border, on Wednesday, a foreign security source based in Ethiopia told AFP, while a TPLF source said they had seized several other towns in Afar. The foreign security source also said there was fighting around the Amhara town of Weldiya – one of the few routes to the capital. cards.source_title: Rebel offensive against Ethiopian army stokes fears of return to civil war

cards.title: 调查揭露特朗普政府与多国秘密达成驱逐协议，数千移民被送往陌生国度

entities.name: USAID（美国国际开发署）
entities.explain: 美国政府负责对外援助的机构，特朗普政府已大幅削减其项目和预算

entities.name: 秘密驱逐协议
entities.explain: 美国与数十个国家私下达成的安排，将移民遣送至这些国家，而非其原籍国

cards.summary: 《卫报》深度调查揭露，特朗普政府与数十个国家达成秘密协议，将数千名移民驱逐至他们从未听说过的第三国。一名伊朗女性在戴着手铐的飞机上才通过座位屏幕得知目的地是非洲某国。这些行动耗费美国纳税人数百万美元，被批评为'武力展示'。
cards.relevant: 该调查揭示了美国移民政策的重大转变——将移民遣送至与原籍无关的第三国，引发国际法和人权方面的严重争议。
cards.context: 特朗普政府上台后大幅收紧移民政策，在遣返原籍国拒绝接收的情况下，转而与第三国谈判达成接收协议，将移民送往非洲等地。这一做法绕过了常规遣返程序的法律审查。
cards.source_analysis: 《卫报》以调查报道见长，对特朗普政府移民政策持批评立场，此报道基于对当事人的采访和文件调查。
cards.social_impact: 数千名移民被遣送至陌生国家，面临语言不通、无社会关系网络、法律地位不明等困境。行动耗费美国纳税人数百万美元。
cards.source_text: Nika’s story No one would tell the shackled detainees onboard the US immigration plane where they were going. The officers in charge would taunt them when they asked, they said. It was only when the seat-back video screens finally showed a map that the 18 migrants worked it out. Their destination was Central African Republic (CAR), a country few of them had even heard of. Nika, a 32-year-old Iranian woman, recalled how the handcuffs dug into her wrists. She begged the officers to loosen them, but they did not. Other passengers had it worse, she said. Some of the men were restrained in black and yellow body wraps, as if mummified, after resisting orders to get on the plane. Nika, who had fled Iran 18 months earlier after protesting against its regime, had imagined the US as a place of sanctuary. Iran was already one of the most repressive countries in the world when she left, and its horrors had only deepened since then: security forces gunned down thousands of other demonstrators this year, then Donald Trump’s administration launched the war there. After more than a year locked up in a US immigration detention centre, Nika, whose name the Guardian has changed to protect her family in Iran, was granted legal protections and freed on a judge’s orders. Within two weeks, the Department of Homeland Security had rearrested her, and days later she was on the plane heading 7,000 miles east. “They never told me they were going to deport me [to] this country,” she told the Guardian. “I don’t know anything about Africa.” The Department of State warns US citizens not to travel to CAR because it says it is too dangerous. Nika spends most of her days there under a form of self-imprisonment, too scared to venture out from her small bedroom as she waits for an answer to the question on which her life depends: will she be sent back to Iran, and to a regime that could kill her? Nika is one of more than 25,000 people deported by the Trump administration to countries that are not their own. About 20,000 people have been bussed to Mexico, according to a count by Refugees International and Human Rights First. And more than 5,000 others have been put on flights to countries in Africa, Latin America, the Caribbean and central Asia to which they have no connection, and then, often, returned to the countries where US immigration judges had ruled their lives or liberty were at risk. cards.source_title: Banished to alien lands: Trump’s secret deportation deals

cards.title: 内塔尼亚胡在联合国演讲中为以色列军事行动辩护，多国代表集体退场

entities.name: 本雅明·内塔尼亚胡
entities.explain: 以色列总理，长期执政的右翼领导人，当前因加沙战争面临国际压力

entities.name: 联合国大会
entities.explain: 联合国最高级别的全体会议，每年9月各国领导人齐聚纽约发表演讲

cards.summary: 以色列总理内塔尼亚胡在联合国大会发表演讲，为以色列在中东的军事行动辩护，并将退场的代表称为'道德懦夫'。数十名外交官在他登台时集体走出会场，以示对以色列军事行动的抗议。
cards.relevant: 联合国大会上的集体退场是罕见的外交抗议形式，反映出国际社会对以色列加沙军事行动的分歧日益加深。
cards.context: 自2023年10月哈马斯袭击以色列以来，以军在加沙的军事行动已持续近一年，造成大量平民伤亡，多国对其行动合法性提出质疑。内塔尼亚胡此次演讲旨在在国际舞台上为以色列立场争取支持。
cards.source_analysis: BBC报道以事实陈述为主，中立呈现事件经过，未明显偏向任何一方。
cards.social_impact: 数十国代表退场显示以色列在国际社会中的孤立程度加深，可能影响其后续外交空间和军事行动的國際合法性。
cards.source_text: Netanyahu defends Israeli military action as delegates walk out before UN speech - Published Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has fiercely defended his country's military campaigns in Iran, Gaza and elsewhere in the Middle East in a speech to the UN General Assembly. After dozens of delegates walked out in protest as he took to the stage, Netanyahu vowed to continue fighting: "We're going to win. We have no other choice." In response to the walkout, he said: "If there are any other moral cowards who haven't left the hall, please do so now." The Israeli leader also rejected accusations that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza. Hours earlier, in a recorded message Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas told the UN that Israeli policies - in particular the illegal expansion of Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank - threatened "the very life and existence of the Palestinian people on their homeland". He also said it jeopardised the two-state solution, which is an internationally backed formula for peace between Israel and the Palestinians. Abbas said that Palestinians were being subjected to "killing, destruction, starvation and attempts at displacement, as well as a genocidal war" in Gaza by the Israeli military. The Palestinian leader was addressing the annual gathering via a video link because had been denied a US entry visa. Netanyahu, who is subject to an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for alleged war crimes, launched scathing attacks on nations and leaders who have criticised him. "They accuse Israel, tiny Israel, of colonialism - some colonialism. And who's accusing us? Among them are people in Britain and in France. For God's sake, they invented the term," he said. He went on to label Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan a "tyrant", accusing him of supporting the Palestinian armed group Hamas. Erdogan told the UN on Tuesday that the injustices faced by those in Gaza and the West Bank "deeply offends the conscience of humanity". New York City's left-wing mayor Zohran Mamdani - who had previously vowed to arrest Netanyahu but later said he did not have the authority to do so - was also criticised by the Israeli leader. "Since you were elected mayor of this city, many Jews no longer feel safe in New York," the Israeli prime minister said. In a statement, Mamdani's office said Netanyahu "used his speech to repeat baseless lies meant to sanitize his genocide of Palestinians". Netanyahu also thanked US President Donald Trump fo
cards.source_title: Netanyahu defends Israeli military action as delegates walk out before UN speech

entities.explain: 纽约市市长，内塔尼亚胡在演讲中点名攻击的对象

entities.name: 联合国大会
entities.explain: 联合国最高级别的全体会议，各国领导人每年9月齐聚纽约

cards.summary: 内塔尼亚胡在联合国大会发表强硬演讲，为以色列在中东各地的军事行动辩护，同时攻击纽约市长马姆达尼等批评者。数十名代表在他登台时集体退场。演讲凸显以色列与联合国多数成员国之间的深刻裂痕。
cards.relevant: 内塔尼亚胡在演讲中攻击美国国内政治人物（纽约市长），显示以色列与美国地方政府层面的关系也在恶化。
cards.context: 加沙战争持续近一年，以色列在联合国的处境日益孤立。内塔尼亚胡选择在联大这一全球最大外交舞台上采取强硬姿态，而非寻求缓和。
cards.source_analysis: 《纽约时报》以'好斗'形容内塔尼亚胡的演讲，报道侧重其攻击性言辞和现场反应，立场偏向自由派读者群。
cards.social_impact: 数十名代表退场是联大近年来罕见的外交抗议场面，反映以色列在国际多边舞台上的孤立加剧。

Live Updates: Netanyahu Lashes Out at Critics and Underscores Threats to Israel。In a combative speech, the prime minister defended Israeli military action across the Middle East, and attacked Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York. Dozens of delegates walked out of the hall as he took the podium.

cards.title: 特朗普与习近平白宫会晤，但AI合作前景依然渺茫

entities.name: 习近平
entities.explain: 中国国家主席，中国最高领导人

entities.name: 特朗普
entities.explain: 美国总统，2025年重返白宫后推行对华竞争与交易并行的政策

entities.name: 海军陆战队一号
entities.explain: 美国总统专用的直升机，用于短途出行

cards.summary: 美国总统特朗普在白宫椭圆形办公室与中国国家主席习近平举行会谈。特朗普亲自带习近平参观白宫，包括海军陆战队一号直升机和新建停机坪。尽管会晤气氛友好，但双方在人工智能领域的合作前景依然不被看好。
cards.relevant: 中美作为全球AI两大强国，其合作或对抗将决定全球AI治理格局。此次会晤虽展示个人外交，但实质性合作未见突破。
cards.context: 中美关系在贸易、技术、台海等问题上持续紧张。特朗普以个人化外交风格著称，此次以高规格接待习近平，但双方在AI等关键技术领域的竞争态势未变。
cards.source_analysis: France24为法国公共国际新闻频道，报道侧重会晤的象征性场面，对AI合作前景持审慎态度。
cards.social_impact: 中美AI合作若持续停滞，将加速全球技术阵营分化，影响AI标准制定、芯片供应链和全球科技治理。

Issued on: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump have been holding talks in the Oval Office at the White House today. President Donald Trump gave the visiting leader of communist China a personal tour of several of his favorite White House features. He took him aboard the Marine One helicopter, presented the new granite landing pad he had built for it, and pointed out the massive adjacent construction site where a ballroom will eventually stand. It's been a busy schedule for the two leaders that will culimate in a state dinner which will be attended by CEOs of top AI companies, including OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk. Well earlier Xi told his US counterpart that AI must remain “under human control”. It comes as AI leaders have sounded the alarm in recent weeks that the technology is too fast. Meanwhile China and the United States are locked in an A.I. race, Trump has dismissed calls for stricter controls, claiming AI fears are a “hoax”.

cards.title: 法官下令后白宫恢复被特朗普封禁媒体的采访权限

entities.name: CNN
entities.explain: 美国主流有线新闻频道，长期被特朗普批评为'假新闻'

cards.summary: 在联邦法官下达命令后，白宫恢复了CNN、Politico和MS NOW等媒体的采访权限。此前这些媒体的工作人员被拒绝进入白宫采访。此举被视为对新闻自由的一次司法胜利。
cards.relevant: 白宫限制特定媒体采访权限涉及宪法第一修正案新闻自由问题，司法介入具有重要判例意义。
cards.context: 特朗普政府此前以各种理由禁止部分批评他的媒体进入白宫采访，引发新闻自由争议。相关媒体提起诉讼后，联邦法官裁定白宫必须恢复其采访权限。
cards.source_analysis: BBC以中立立场报道司法裁决结果，未对特朗普政府或媒体任何一方做明显倾向性评价。
cards.social_impact: 此案确立了对白宫限制媒体采访权的司法审查标准，可能影响未来政府与媒体关系的边界。
cards.source_text: White House restores access to media outlets banned by Trump after judge's order - Published CNN, Politico and MS NOW are back in the White House, hours after a federal judge ruled President Donald Trump's ban on the three news outlets was probably unconstitutional and ordered their access immediately restored. The outlets sought an emergency court hearing to regain entry accusing the White House in a court filing of having "repeatedly violated" the judge's ruling by turning away their journalists. The hearing was called off after access was restored. Trump initially said he barred the outlets because of "fake news". The White House later cited national security. But in his overnight ruling, Judge Timothy Kelly cast doubt on the claim about national security concerns. The chaotic standoff limited some TV coverage as Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House ahead of a state dinner later. Judge Kelly ruled the ban on the outlets should be temporarily lifted because it "likely violated their constitutional due process rights". CNN, Politico and MS Now all reported being denied entry to the White House on Thursday morning, prompting their request for an emergency hearing. In response, the director of White House Operations said in a court filing that the press passes and confiscated badges had been restored by 09:45. Shortly afterwards, all three outlets said they were allowed back in. However, networks including Fox News, NBC, CBS and ABC, which pulled out in solidarity, have yet to confirm they will resume broadcast coverage from the White House. - Judge dismisses Trump lawsuit against Iowa newspaper and pollster over 2024 race - Published8 hours ago Judge Kelly ruled CNN, Politico and MS NOW were "likely to succeed" in showing the White House had not exercised "adequate due process" in the ban. The judge also rejected the argument that national security concerns underpinned the exclusion, pointing out the president made no mention of this in his initial announcement. "The record lacks factual support for defendants' contention that the revocation of plaintiffs' hard passes will in fact protect national security," Kelly wrote. He ordered the immediate return of the outlets' press passes and a halt to enforcement of the ban for 14 days. In a court filing on Tuesday, the US Department of Justice had accused the news outlets of threatening national security with their coverage. cards.summary: 澳大利亚在联合国大会上宣布发现OpenAI存在安全漏洞。澳大利亚此前已实施严格的社交媒体限制，并提出对算法和智能眼镜的管控方案。选择联大这一全球最大政治舞台公布此事，显示其推动AI国际监管的意图。
cards.relevant: 澳大利亚将AI安全漏洞提升至联合国层面，可能推动形成AI安全事件的国际通报机制和监管框架。
cards.context: 澳大利亚近年来在科技监管方面走在前列，已通过未成年人社交媒体禁令并提议算法透明度要求。此次在联大披露OpenAI漏洞，是其将国内监管议程推向国际舞台的举措。
cards.source_analysis: BBC报道侧重澳大利亚选择联大作为披露场合的战略考量，未对OpenAI漏洞本身的技术细节做深入分析。
cards.social_impact: 若AI安全漏洞成为国际议题，可能加速全球AI监管协调，影响OpenAI等公司的国际运营合规成本。
cards.source_text: Why Australia chose the world's biggest political stage to reveal OpenAI hack - Published Australia made a dramatic revelation on Wednesday during the United Nations General Assembly. Rogue AI agents had hacked one of its government bodies - the first known incident of its kind in the world. Private data, but not sensitive information, was taken from Medicare, Australia's universal healthcare scheme. The breach happened in June, but OpenAI says it only became aware of it in August - and then took until 10 September to alert Australia's government, by sending an email to an address used by researchers and academics to alert authorities to concerns of vulnerabilities. While worrying, the timing of the incident is somewhat of a gift for Australia. A middle power that doesn't usually get as much of a platform as its influential allies, the country wants to be seen as punching above its weight on one of the most defining issues of our time - big tech regulation. In the past year alone, it has implemented the world's strictest social media ban, announced what it says are the world's strongest algorithm controls, floated the possibility of "world-leading" limits on smart glasses, and is now the first government to confront AI firms over a rogue attack on its data. It's entirely possible other governments have been the victim of rogue AI agents. Former Australian government cybersecurity adviser Alastair MacGibbon told the BBC he'd heard whispers that several others have been notified of similar recent breaches by OpenAI agents. "Some have chosen to not be public – that's every government's choice on how it wants to handle these things," the CyberCX chief strategy officer said. "The [Australian] government chose a time to release this to gain maximum publicity which is their wont to do." Revealing a data breach can of course be a risky strategy for governments - it leaves them vulnerable to criticism that their security systems aren't up to scratch. But the fact that no sensitive information was leaked put Australia in a stronger position to use the incident. "Nobody has died," says the University of Queensland's associate professor Michael Noetel, who studies AI risks. "This is another canary in the coal mine. This sort of loss-of-control incident, even though it's minor now, is what CEOs are worried about getting worse over time." cards.source_text: The United States’ withdrawal from key aid programs has put healthcare in Africa and the global south “under growing strain” a new report warns. The report says the Trump administration’s cuts to programs such as US Agency for International Development (USAID), as well as the Covid-19 pandemic and rising costs of living globally have brought “new urgency” for the need to reform healthcare in the region. The report, titled A Sovereign Future For Health, was created by the Accra Reset, a global health initiative led by John Dramani Mahama, Ghana’s president, that believes countries in Africa and the wider global south should have greater control over their health development rather than being dependent on aid from western countries and international institutions. A key statistic cited by Mahama and Accra Reset is that Africa produces less than 1% of its vaccines while carrying about 25% of the global disease burden. The report cites how abrupt changes to global health financing, such as the US withdrawal from several global health initiatives, forced countries within the global south to urgently restructure their finances. The report points to the Trump administration’s decision to dissolve USAID, which pushed Nigeria to absorb the 28,000 health workers who were previously employed by the agency at a cost of $200m. External financing for health in Africa contracted by close to 70% between 2021 and 2025, the report notes, meaning that African countries historically dependent on aid were forced to adapt quickly. The withdrawal of the US Emergency Plan for Aids Relief (Pepfar) funding for South Africa, which provided over $400m a year annually and is credited with saving 26m lives globally since 2003, led to HIV clinics closing across the country. That left 1.4 million people living with HIV to face uncertainty about their treatment. Such funding cuts caused “severe and devastating” disruption globally, according to research presented at the 26th International Aids Conference in Brazil earlier this year. At the World Health Assembly in May, Mahama said Ghana lost $78m after the closure of USAID programs which affected maternal healthcare, the treatment of malaria, nutrition and HIV/Aids interventions. The initiative’s latest report, published on Monday, comes amid these major cuts to international aid and growing pressure on countries to take greater ownership of their health systems. cards.source_text: A payments business that operates across Africa and is ultimately controlled by an Indian billionaire has announced its intention to float on the struggling London Stock Exchange. Airtel Money, the mobile money arm of Airtel Africa, is planning one of the biggest UK listings in years, in a boost for the shrinking London market that has faced a string of recent departures. The company is understood to be hoping to raise about $800m (£601m) from the initial public offering (IPO) and is targeting a valuation of $8bn to $9bn, which would make it one of London’s largest listings in recent years. Airtel Money has 53 million monthly active users across 13 countries in sub-Saharan Africa, including Uganda, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo. It operates through a network of branches and kiosks, which enable customers to load money on to their phones, withdraw cash and access other money services, and the company generated revenues of just under $1.4bn in the last financial year. Airtel Money’s parent company is Airtel Africa, a telecoms provider that is part of the Indian conglomerate Bharti Enterprises, which is ultimately controlled by the billionaire Sunil Bharti Mittal. Airtel Africa is already listed on the FTSE 100 but said it wanted Airtel Money to be listed separately. “From a company perspective, [the listing] gives us flexibility for the future,” said Airtel Money’s chief executive, Ian Ferrao. “We evaluated multiple [stock] exchanges, including the Middle East because we’ve got a headquarters in Dubai, along with European and North American exchanges. Ultimately, shareholders felt that London was the right choice. We still believe there is deep capital available … all the global institutional investors are here.” Ferrao added: “Most importantly there’s a deep understanding of emerging markets in the London market and Africa specifically.” Airtel Money said it would announce more details about the float in early October, including the indicative price range and number of shares to be offered, with final pricing to follow later in the month. Airtel Africa had originally targeted a listing in the first six months of 2026 but delayed it to the second half of the year, blaming unfavourable market conditions as a result of the US-Israeli war on Iran. Several other companies also pushed back planned IPOs amid the market volatility caused by the conflict. Airtel Africa owns just under 78% of Airtel Money and will remain a long-term investor after the I
cards.source_title: Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in years

cards.source_text: Four civilians killed in Pakistani strikes in Afghanistan, Taliban says - Published Afghanistan's Taliban government said a wave of Pakistani air strikes had killed four civilians in the latest escalation between the two sides. The strikes hit provinces including Kandahar, the Taliban's base of power, sources told the BBC. A resident told AFP news agency they heard a jet, followed by a large explosion and then a fire in the city. Pakistan said its forces had struck 10 targets in Afghanistan, without specifying their locations, adding the strikes were "strictly limited to identified military objectives". It's the second wave of Pakistani air strikes on Afghan territory in the past week, and comes after a deadly attack on a police facility in Pakistan on 18 September. In a statement, the Taliban said there would be an "appropriate response" following the attack, while Pakistan said any further "provocative act" would be responded to. Taliban government spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid said the attacks were in Afghanistan's Kandahar, Paktia and Khost provinces. In Paktia, an official said jets had bombed the Afghan Armed Forces' 203 Mansouri Corps, which is controlled by the Taliban, without providing any information on casualties. In Khost, a spokesman said houses were damaged in the strikes, with no casualties reported. Abdullah, a local eyewitness, told Reuters news agency the strikes happened around midnight. "People were shouting, and there was panic all around," he said. "Afterwards, the village elder arrived and called out to the houses, asking if anyone was killed. Thankfully, no one was killed." Another local, Salamat Khan, told Reuters that "there is no military base here, nor are there any military personnel", adding "there are only the homes of ordinary civilians". Zabihullah Mujahid labelled the attack as "reckless, careless, and hostile", and said it "will have adverse consequences for the Pakistani military". Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the strikes were "deliberate, precise, calibrated, and proportionate, and strictly limited to identified military objectives directly linked to the attempted attacks against Pakistan". The Taliban and Pakistan had enjoyed three months of relative calm, until fighting reignited following an attack on a mosque at a police compound in north-western Pakistan last week, which killed at least 31 people, according to AFP. France will send troops and defence systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu, which is key for energy transport, French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday. Macron also said a US ban on diesel exports, which the White House has denied is under consideration, would be "catastrophic", both globally and for the US economy. Read moreFrance to send 'military means' to protect key Saudi oil port Macron was speaking in a wide-ranging primetime television interview on the international situation, in which he also warned about possible Russian attacks on French soil. Facing growing pressure at home over high energy prices, Macron sought to assure the French that France had adequate gas and oil supplies as winter approaches. He said Paris was actively working to ensure flows were not disrupted. Crude oil prices have surged recently as the main alternative route for Saudi oil exports through Yanbu has come under missile attacks from Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis. "We are going to send military resources, that is to say, soldiers, radar systems and defence systems, to protect this site – not to get us involved in any conflicts, but to protect this site," Macron told TF1 and France 2 TV. Germany said Russia was responsible for an attempted drone attack in August on the Leipzig airport. cards.source_text: MEXICO, September 25. /TASS/. The government of Colombia has made the decision to sever diplomatic ties with Iran, accusing Tehran of "presumed ties to international terrorist groups." "The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, on behalf of the Government of Colombia, announces that <…> it has formally severed diplomatic relations with the Islamic Republic of Iran," reads a statement, published by the country’s Foreign Ministry. cards.source_text: Hundreds of thousands expected in Paris for Pope's visit - Published Pope Leo XIV embarks on a four-day visit to France on Friday, with the highpoint being a giant Mass attended by more than half a million people in central Paris. For Saturday's afternoon celebration, an altar has been built on the Place de la Concorde and a large area around the Champs-Élysées sealed off by police. Some 600,000 Catholic faithful are expected to cram the avenue up to the Arc de Triomphe and beyond. Large crowds are also due at other stages in the Pope's itinerary, reflecting an enthusiasm that the Church attributes to growing spiritual thirst among the French and other Europeans. President Emmanuel Macron will greet the Pope at Orly airport on Friday morning, and then hold talks with him at the Élysée Palace on geopolitical issues and artificial intelligence (AI). He will also deliver a speech with the Pope in Metz. However, the president will not be at any of the Pope's Masses, largely to avoid breaching France's strict separation of state and religion. Instead, the Champs-Élysées Mass will be attended by his wife Brigitte and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu. Several candidates for next year's presidential election are also due, including Marine Le Pen of the nationalist right, centrists Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal, and conservative Bruno Retailleau. There were reports of tensions between Macron and the Vatican team sent to make arrangements, with the president allegedly frustrated in his wish for a more ceremonial aspect to the visit. This was dismissed this week by Élysée officials, who said it was customary to offer a visiting head of state – which the Pope is – a range of high-profile events, such as a cavalry escort down the Champs-Élysées. But they said it was never expected that the Pope would actually take the offer up. They did confirm that Pope Leo turned down Macron's idea of a meeting with artisans who helped rebuild the fire-devastated Notre-Dame cathedral. This was because his agenda was too tight, they said. After a Popemobile ride through crowds to Notre-Dame cathedral on Friday afternoon, Pope Leo XIV will be joined in the evening by 80,000 young people at the Stade de France in northern Paris. On Sunday 150,000 have signed up to attend mass in the Pyrenean sanctuary of Lourdes. cards.relevant: 事件涉及美丹关系、格陵兰地缘政治以及社交媒体虚假信息传播，反映了当前国际外交中的舆论战现象。
cards.context: 特朗普曾提出购买格陵兰岛引发丹麦不满。卢比奥作为美国国务卿出席格陵兰相关签约仪式时，现场播放了《Send in the Clowns》，该歌曲名称被解读为对美方的讽刺。
cards.source_analysis: France24是法国国际新闻频道，其事实核查栏目对视频真实性进行了独立验证，立场偏向澄清事实而非煽动情绪。

Issued on: Modified: A viral video claims Danish officials played Judy Collins’ “Send in the Clowns” as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived for a Greenland signing ceremony, sparking claims of Danish “trolling”. Our checks of separate livestreams confirm the song really played and the video was not manipulated. Denmark has denied choosing the music, while the UN says it did not organise the event. Whilst the song was real, there is no evidence Denmark selected it deliberately. Vedika Bahl fact-checks. On the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, the United States, Denmark and Greenland signed a deal Tuesday to expand Washington’s military presence in the Arctic territory. The agreement came after months of diplomatic tensions over Greenland, with Denmark also seeking to reaffirm its control over the island. But an unusual song played before the signing has sparked a wave of speculation online. A video circulating widely on social media claims Danish officials deliberately played Judy Collins’ version of the classic Broadway song “Send in the Clowns” as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived. The clip has amassed more than a million views in a single post on X, with the footage also widely shared on Bluesky, Threads, Facebook and Instagram. The song’s lyrics include the line: “Where are the clowns? Send in the clowns. Don't bother, they're here.” Social media users quickly interpreted the music as a deliberate dig at the US delegation, with some praising Denmark for what they described as “epic trolling”. Others questioned whether the footage was genuine, while some went further, sharing AI-generated images depicting members of the US delegation as clowns. The speculation raised a key question: did the song actually play at the ceremony, and if so, was it deliberately chosen by Denmark? We checked footage from multiple livestreams of the event. The original viral video carries the watermark of US-based outlet MAGNO News. In its Facebook livestream, just before the 11-minute mark, Rubio and other delegates can be seen entering as “Send in the Clowns” plays in the background.
